An object is more stable when its centre of gravity is low and its base of support is wide. It topples when the line of action of its weight falls outside its base of support. For example, a cone on its base returns after a slight tilt; widening an object's base makes toppling less likely.

Stability can be improved by lowering an object's centre of gravity and widening its base of support. For example, racing cars are designed to be low and broad, and balancing toys have their weight concentrated low down.
